issue.title: Raise sase-core-rs floor for notification snooze contract
issue.description: Primary dependency metadata can resolve a core version older than the notification snooze implementation.

fields.description: Current primary HEAD 661699f38 includes notification snooze/resurface behavior backed by sase-core v0.17.6 lineage, but pyproject.toml and uv.lock still allow sase-core-rs>=0.17.4 and the lock resolves 0.17.4. After just install built the refreshed linked v0.17.6 core, uv run pytest auto-synced the environment back to 0.17.4; 11 notification snooze, resurfaced_at, catalog-ordering, and facade tests then failed deterministically in isolation. Raise the minimum/locked core version to the first release containing a856b66 and verify both normal uv sync and just check use the compatible binding.

payload.close_reason: Waiting to see if an epic lander agent handles this.

payload.entry: Raised the main sase-core-rs dependency floor to >=0.17.5,<0.18.0 and regenerated uv.lock, which now resolves published sase-core-rs 0.17.7 instead of 0.17.4. Proved the minimum supported wheel by temporarily installing published sase-core-rs==0.17.5 into the main venv, confirming importlib.metadata version 0.17.5, then passing 43 focused facade/catalog/mobile tests plus all 69 tests/notification_store tests including test_snooze_e2e_matrix. Restored the linked development core with just install and confirmed installed sase-core-rs 0.17.7. Follow-up verification passed: main notification/ACE/CLI/mobile/sort/E2E matrix 268 passed; main just install && just check passed after updating the dependency-floor smoke assertion and accepting the already-tracked Config Center populated-tab golden; linked sase-core cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace passed; linked sase-telegram standalone just install && just check reproduced the known old-published-sase adapter mismatch, then the current main/core environment passed just check with 516 tests including all four snooze-resurface E2E tests.
